# The problem {#sec-eikonal-problem}

This document describes how each manufactured solution of the
eikonal--diffusion equation used by cardiacFoam is built. In the method of
manufactured solutions [@roache2002code] an exact field is chosen first and the
source that makes it satisfy the equation is derived from it. The document
gives the exact activation times, the sources that make them exact, the reference values of the
eikonal-driven ECG and the checks that each construction passes before
anything is written. It states the problems only; it contains no solver
output. Every displayed field, source and coefficient below is printed by the
sympy generator that also writes the NumPy reference module and, for
cardiacFoam, the C++ reference header, so the document, the references and the
solver cannot disagree. A reader with this document and the generator folder
can rebuild each problem in another code.

## Domain and governing equations

The activation time $\psi(\mathbf x)$ solves the anisotropic
eikonal--diffusion equation [@collifranzone1990eikonal; @jacquemet2012eikonal]
in the myocardium $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$,

$$
-\nabla\cdot(\mathbf M\nabla\psi)
+c_0\sqrt{\nabla\psi\cdot\mathbf M\nabla\psi}
=1+S_\psi,
\qquad
\mathbf M=\frac{\boldsymbol{\sigma}}{\chi C_m},
$$

where $S_\psi$ is the manufactured source ($S_\psi=0$ in ordinary runs) and $c_0$, in
s$^{-1/2}$, is a scaling coefficient rather than a conduction velocity.
Ordinary runs seal the walls, $\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf M\nabla\psi=0$, and
prescribe $\psi=0$ at the stimulus sites. Each manufactured problem states its
own boundary and interior constraints: the Cartesian cube prescribes the exact
$\psi$ on the boundary, and the shell seals both walls and pins a small ball of
cells about the stimulus point. The source is the residual of the operator on
the exact field,
$S_\psi=-\nabla\cdot(\mathbf M\nabla\psi)+c_0\sqrt{\nabla\psi\cdot\mathbf M\nabla\psi}-1$.

The normalised cases use the solver's dimensional convention: $\psi$ in s,
$\mathbf M$ in m$^2$ s$^{-1}$ and $c_0$ in s$^{-1/2}$, with the fields written
on the normalised coordinates $x/(1\,\mathrm m)$, so the arguments of the
exponential and square-root functions are dimensionless.

The eikonal-driven ECG observes $\psi$ through a transmembrane template
$U$ [@pezzuto2017rapid]: $V_m(\mathbf x,t)=U(t-\psi(\mathbf x))$, so
$\nabla V_m=-U'(t-\psi)\nabla\psi$, substituted in the pseudo-ECG
functional [@gima2002ionic] with the normalisation $c_{\mathrm{ECG}}=1$.

## Reading and regenerating {#sec-eikonal-regenerate}

The generators live in `tutorials/manufacturedSolutions/generators/` of the
cardiacFoam repository. Each case has one sympy generator `<case>_mms.py` that
writes `reference/<case>.py`, a NumPy-only module with the exact fields,
sources and reference quadratures, and `latex/<case>_*.tex`, the fragments
printed in this document. Set up the environment once and run a generator
from that folder:

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
.venv/bin/python cartesian_eikonal_mms.py --emit
.venv/bin/python cartesian_eikonal_mms.py --self-check
```

`--emit` runs the self-checks first and writes nothing if one fails;
`--self-check` runs them alone. The generators that own a cardiacFoam header
also take `--check PATH` and `--write PATH`, needed only by cardiacFoam
developers. The document is built with

```bash
quarto render docs/eikonal/eikonal_mms.qmd --to pdf
```

and its figures with `python docs/eikonal/figures.py`.

{{< include ../_common/creating.qmd >}}

# Cartesian eikonal field {#sec-cartesian}

## Description and limitations

An exponential activation time on the unit cube $[0,1]^d$, $d=1,2,3$, with a
constant conductivity tensor, full or diagonal. The case exercises the
interior discretisation of the eikonal--diffusion operator: the metric term,
the anisotropic diffusion term with a full tensor, the cell-gradient
reconstruction and the outer nonlinear iteration.

The exact $\psi$ is prescribed on every face and on the cells whose centre has
the smallest $x$, $y$ or $z$, so the case exercises neither a sealed wall,
nor the zero-gradient outer boundary of ordinary runs, nor the placement of
internal stimulus sites. The tensor is constant, so its derivatives do not
enter the source.

## Problem instance

Unit cube $[0,1]^d$ with

{{< include ../../latex/eikonal_params.tex >}}

and one of the two tensors of the tutorial,

{{< include ../../latex/eikonal_sigma_rotated.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/eikonal_sigma_axis.tex >}}

In cardiacFoam this is the tutorial `eikonal/cube` (`-conductivity rotated`, the
default, or `axis`; `-dim 1|2|3`) with the verifier
`manufacturedEikonalVerifier`.

## Construction

The field is the exponential of a linear form,

{{< include ../../latex/eikonal_kd.tex >}}

chosen because it reproduces itself under differentiation:
$\nabla\psi=\mathbf k_d\psi$. With $\mathbf M$ constant,
$\nabla\psi\cdot\mathbf M\nabla\psi=K_M\psi^2$ and
$\nabla\cdot(\mathbf M\nabla\psi)=K_M\psi$, so with $\psi>0$ the left-hand side
of the equation equals $\psi(c_0\sqrt{K_M}-K_M)$ and the source follows in
closed form. The construction requires $K_M>0$; a tensor that is not positive
along $\mathbf k_d$ is rejected (the C++ verifier rejects
$K_M\le10^{-300}$).

## Exact solution

{{< include ../../latex/eikonal_psi_d1.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/eikonal_psi_d2.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/eikonal_psi_d3.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/eikonal_gradpsi.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/eikonal_KM.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/eikonal_source.tex >}}

The full expressions are `fields(d, sigma, chi, cm, c0)` of
`cartesian_eikonal_mms.py`, and `tau_d<d>`, `grad_tau_d<d>`, `source_d<d>` and
the checked wrapper `source(d, point, sigma, c0, chi, cm)` of
`reference/cartesian_eikonal.py`.

## Self-checks

`--self-check` asserts that the residual of the eikonal equation with the
source vanishes to $10^{-12}$ at a sample point for $d=1,2,3$, for both
tutorial tensors and for $c_0\in\{1,5,66\}$; and that a tensor with $K_M=0$ is
rejected.

# Eikonal-driven ECG {#sec-eikonal-ecg}

## Description and limitations

The eikonal-driven ECG of the Cartesian field of @sec-cartesian: the
pseudo-ECG functional of the template voltage $V_m=U(t-\psi)$ at electrodes
outside the cube. The case exercises the chain from the computed activation
time through its reconstructed gradient and the template to the functional;
its reference uses the exact gradient $\nabla\psi=\mathbf k_d\psi$. The
reference is a quadrature of the exact integrand, not a closed form. The
generator covers the cube; the shell ECG reference of cardiacFoam
(`domain shell`) is the same integrand over the shell of @sec-eikonal-shell, computed
by the verifier from the shell header and not part of the emitted modules.
The sine template repeats many times across the activation range, so its
integrand changes sign many times over the cube and the integral cancels to a
small fraction of the sum of the magnitudes of its terms.

## Problem instance

Two templates: a single smooth event and a sine. The single event is

{{< include ../../latex/eikonal_ecg_template_U.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/eikonal_ecg_template_H.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/eikonal_ecg_template_w.tex >}}

so that $H$ rises from 10% to 90% within the rise time $T_r$, with

{{< include ../../latex/eikonal_ecg_params.tex >}}

The duration $D$ exceeds the activation range $e^3-1$ of $d=3$, so
$U'(t-\psi)$ keeps one sign across the cube. The sine template is

{{< include ../../latex/eikonal_ecg_template_sine_U.tex >}}

In cardiacFoam:

- the ECG of the tutorial `eikonal/cube`;
- verifier `manufacturedEikonalECGVerifier`;
- `template singleEvent` (the default) or `template sine`.

## Construction

With $\mathbf r=\mathbf x-\mathbf r_e$, and in $d<3$ only the first $d$
coordinates of $\mathbf r$, the functional is the integral over $[0,1]^d$ of

{{< include ../../latex/eikonal_ecg_integrand.tex >}}

with $U'$ evaluated at $t-\psi(\mathbf x)$. With
$a=\tanh(s/w)$ and $b=\tanh((s-D)/w)$, the template derivatives are

{{< include ../../latex/eikonal_ecg_template_ab.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/eikonal_ecg_template_single_event.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/eikonal_ecg_template_sine.tex >}}

## Exact solution

The reference $\Phi_e(\mathbf r_e,t)$ is a tensor-product Gauss--Legendre
quadrature with $q_{\mathrm{ref}}$ points per axis on $[0,1]^d$. The functional
has no separate time factor: the time enters through $U'(t-\psi)$ at every
quadrature point. The NumPy module holds
`integrand_d<d>_<template>(x, y, z, t, ex, ey, ez, sxx, sxy, sxz, syy, syz, szz, duration, rise)`,
`template_derivative_single_event`, `template_derivative_sine` and
`spatial_reference(d, template, sigma, electrode, t, order, duration, rise)`.

*Note for implementers.* The tutorial uses $q_{\mathrm{ref}}=48$. The
integrand is set to 0 where $\lVert\mathbf r\rVert^2\le10^{-300}$
($|x-r_{e,x}|\le10^{-300}$ in $d=1$), so an electrode that coincides with a
quadrature point contributes 0, not a non-finite value. Because the quadrature
sum cancels (the functional can be $10^{-6}$ of the sum of the magnitudes of
its terms) and $\tanh$ and $\cos$ are evaluated in a different order by
different codes, two correct implementations agree only to a bound that scales
with those magnitudes, not to a fixed relative tolerance. cardiacFoam compares
its C++ reference with the NumPy reference within
$10^{-12}|\Phi_e|+2\times10^{-13}\sum_q|W_q\,U'\,\kappa|+3\times10^{-15}\sum_q|W_q\,\kappa|$,
with $W_q$ the quadrature weights and $\kappa=\mathbf r\cdot\boldsymbol\sigma\nabla\psi/\lVert\mathbf r\rVert^3$
the kernel at the quadrature points. For the shell, cardiacFoam integrates the
same kernel with $q$ Gauss--Legendre nodes in the radius $|\mathbf x|$ (Jacobian
$|\mathbf x|^2$) and in $\mu=\cos\vartheta$, with $\vartheta$ the polar angle, and $2q$
trapezoid nodes in the azimuth.

## Self-checks

`--self-check` asserts that the integrand equals the Cartesian component form
of the C++ reference for $d=1,2,3$ and both templates, to $10^{-12}$; that it
vanishes at an electrode on the evaluation point; that the reference at a
sample electrode agrees between orders 48 and 96 to $10^{-10}\max(1,|\Phi_e|)$,
an absolute bound for $|\Phi_e|\le1$ and a relative one above; and
that the printed single-event building blocks ($H$, $U$, $w$, $a$, $b$) give
the same $U'$ as the template derivative of the generator and as the
derivative of $U$.

(e, f) The reference $\Phi_e(\mathbf r_e,t)$ of the Cartesian field ($d=3$) at three electrodes for each template. The figure writes $\mathbf e$ for the electrode position $\mathbf r_e$.](figures/eikonal_ecg.png){#fig-eikonal-ecg width=100%}

# Sealed spherical shell {#sec-eikonal-shell}

## Description and limitations

The heart-like shell $r_1<|\mathbf x|<r_2$ with both spheres sealed, the
rotating anisotropic conductivity of the monodomain shell, and an activation
time spreading from a mid-wall stimulus point. The exact $\psi$ has non-zero
normal and tangential gradients on both walls while
$\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf M\nabla\psi=0$ holds there exactly, and its wavefronts
collide on the walls behind the cavity. The case poses the full sealed-wall
problem: curved walls, a rotating anisotropic tensor oblique to both walls,
and a spatially varying metric whose derivatives enter the source. At the
critical points of $\psi$ on the walls the metric
$\sqrt{\nabla\psi\cdot\mathbf M\nabla\psi}$ is not differentiable, so the
source is finite there but not smooth; this is a feature of the solution.

The sealed problem fixes $\psi$ only up to a constant, so the cells near the
stimulus point are pinned to the exact $\psi$: the case does not exercise a
stimulus region or the constraint $\psi=0$ of ordinary runs.

The construction is parametric in $c_0$. The stated problem instance is
$c_0=1$; a higher $c_0$ lies outside the regime in which the solver paper
verifies the shell, and the document makes no statement about it.

## Problem instance

{{< include ../../latex/shell_eikonal_params.tex >}}

with the stimulus point

{{< include ../../latex/shell_eikonal_xs.tex >}}

The verifier
pins the cells whose centre lies within $r_{\mathrm{pin}}$ of $\mathbf x_s$ to
the exact $\psi$ (the nearest cell when the mesh has no centre in that ball)
and imposes no value on a wall. In cardiacFoam this is
`eikonal/sphericalShell` with the verifier
`manufacturedShellEikonalVerifier`; its `Allrun` takes `-c0 <value>`
(default 1). The verifier reads $c_0$ from the case, so the source follows the
value given.

$\boldsymbol\sigma$, the wall normals $\mathbf n_j$ and $d_j$ are those of the
monodomain shell:

{{< include ../../latex/shell_fibre.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_sheet.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_sigma.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_omega.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_n1.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_n2.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_d1.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_d2.tex >}}

*Unsealed field.* The smoothed anisotropic distance from $\mathbf x_s$,
measured in the metric frozen at the stimulus point, divided by $c_0$, with
the smoothing length $\delta$ keeping it differentiable at $\mathbf x_s$:

{{< include ../../latex/shell_eikonal_metric.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_eikonal_Ms.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_eikonal_hhat.tex >}}

*Sealing.* The correction of the monodomain shell, written for the operator
tensor $\mathbf M$:

{{< include ../../latex/shell_eikonal_mj.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_eikonal_m.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_eikonal_field.tex >}}

so that $\mathbf n_j\cdot\mathbf M\nabla\psi=0$ on both spheres.

*Dependence on $c_0$.* $\hat h$ and $m$ both carry the factor $1/c_0$, so
$\psi$ scales as $1/c_0$: its critical points and their types do not depend on
$c_0$, while the source does. The checks can be run at any $c_0$
(`--self-check --c0 VALUE`).

## Exact solution

The source is the residual of the operator on the exact field, including the
derivatives of the spatially varying $\mathbf M$:

{{< include ../../latex/shell_eikonal_source.tex >}}

The expanded $\psi$, $\nabla\psi$ and source are not printed: they are
`expressions()` of `shell_eikonal_mms.py` and `psi`, `gradPsi`, `source` and
`sigma` of `reference/shell_eikonal.py`, functions of $(x,y,z)$ and the
parameters, with `field(name, x, y, z, **overrides)` to evaluate them with the
default parameters; `c0` is one of those parameters.

## Self-checks

`--self-check` (at $c_0=1$, or at `--c0 VALUE`) asserts:

- the stored $\mathbf M_s^{-1}$ inverts $\mathbf M(\mathbf x_s)$ to
  $10^{-12}$, and $|\mathbf x_s|=0.75$;
- sealing: $\max|\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf M\nabla\psi|<10^{-25}$ at 200 points
  of each sphere in 30-digit arithmetic;
- the gradient against central differences of $\psi$ to $10^{-5}$, and the
  source against central differences of the flux to $10^{-6}$;
- $\mathbf n_j\cdot\boldsymbol\sigma\mathbf n_j>0$ over the shell widened by
  0.05, and the source finite at $2\times10^{5}$ points of the shell;
- critical points: on each sphere the Morse count (minima $-$ saddles $+$
  maxima) of $\psi$ is 2, so the wall critical points found are complete;
  every interior critical point lies in the pinned ball; every critical point
  outside the ball is non-degenerate (smallest to largest absolute Hessian
  eigenvalue above $10^{-3}$); the local minima outside the ball have
  $\psi>0$ and the pinned minimum exceeds $-10^{-2}$; the source is finite
  next to every critical point.

`--report [--c0 VALUE]` prints the table of critical points.

# Radial eikonal field around a held ball {#sec-eikonal-radial}

## Description and limitations

The activation time of a wave that spreads from a held ball of radius $R$ to the
sealed wall of a concentric sphere of radius $R_o$, in tissue with the
isotropic metric $\mathbf M=m\mathbf I$. The field depends on the radius alone,
so the eikonal--diffusion operator reduces to an ordinary differential
equation with a closed-form solution. The case has no manufactured source:
$S_\psi=0$, and the exact field solves the equation as ordinary runs pose it.
The wall is sealed, $\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf M\nabla\psi=0$, and the ball takes
the place of the stimulus sites: its cells are seeded at the times of a seed
profile and stay at them until the equation reaches them earlier (the held
ball); with the profile `exact` they stay at the exact field.

The case exercises the curvature of the front, which enters through the term
$2\psi'/r$, the exponential layer in which the field meets the sealed wall,
the held ball, and the path from a one-dimensional graph into the tissue: a
terminal at the centre of the ball seeds its cells through
`eikonalPvjCoupler` with the profile of the case. The seed profiles `flat`,
`front` and `curvedFront` pose three problems whose exact fields differ by a
constant, the value held on the ball.

Because the source is zero and the metric is constant, the case exercises
neither a manufactured source nor the derivatives of a varying metric, and the
ball replaces the stimulus box and the condition $\psi=0$ at the stimulus
sites of ordinary runs. The field is singular at the centre (it has $\log r$
and $1/r$ terms), so the ball has a positive radius. The closed form below
uses the exponential integral and overflows a double when
$\mathrm{Pe}_L(a+1)$, defined below, exceeds about 700; the NumPy reference
evaluates the same field without it and has no such limit. The profile
`curvedFront` needs $a\ge2/\mathrm{Pe}_L$, so that the ball contains the
critical radius defined below. The coupler seeds a sphere, so a stretched
ball (the anisotropic variant of the construction) is held by the verifier
instead, with the `flat` or the `exact` profile.

## Problem instance

A sphere of radius $R_o$ centred at the origin, sealed, around a ball of
radius $R$, the held ball. With $L$ the wall thickness, the scales of the
problem are

{{< include ../../latex/radial_eikonal_scales.tex >}}

with $m=\sigma/(\chi C_m)$ the isotropic metric, $V$ the speed of a plane
front and $\mathrm{Pe}_L=VL/m$ the Péclet number of the problem, the ratio of
the advective to the diffusive term. The symbols of this section ($a$, $b$,
$s$, $w$, $m$, $q$, $W$) are local to it. Two parameters describe the problem,
$\mathrm{Pe}_L$ and $a=R/L$, and the tutorial defaults are

{{< include ../../latex/radial_eikonal_params.tex >}}

The tutorial fixes $L=0.0131\,\mathrm m$, $\sigma=0.4978\,\mathrm{S\,m^{-1}}$,
$\chi=1.4\times10^{5}\,\mathrm m^{-1}$ and $C_m=0.01\,\mathrm{F\,m^{-2}}$, so
that $m=\sigma/1400$, and sets $c_0=\mathrm{Pe}_L\sqrt m/L$ and the terminal
time $T_k=2L/V$ (`terminalTime`). In cardiacFoam:

- tutorial `eikonal/coupled1D3DSphere`, run by `Allrun` with `-N` (cells
  across the wall: gmsh tetrahedra of size $L/N$, default 10), `-PeL`,
  `-ballRatio`, `-seedProfile` (`flat`, `front`, `curvedFront` or `exact`)
  and `-axes "ax ay az"`;
- myocardium solver `eikonalSolver` with
  `eikonalAdvectionDiffusionApproach true`, `sealedHeartBoundary true` and
  `conductivitySource field`;
- verifier `manufacturedRadialEikonalVerifier`, which reads `wallThickness`,
  `ballRatio`, `terminalTime`, `sigma`, `axes` and `angle` from the case and
  requires the conductivity that `setManufacturedFields` writes: $\sigma$
  times the identity here, and the tensor of the anisotropic variant below;
- for `flat`, `front` and `curvedFront`, a graph of one edge that leads from
  a root to a terminal at the centre and an `eikonalPvjCoupler` with
  `pvjRadius` equal to $R$, which seeds the cells of the ball at $T_k$ plus the
  offset of the profile (the seed offsets below); for `exact`, no graph: the
  verifier holds the ball at the exact field.

The verifier compares the computed field with the exact one on the cells
outside the ball and reports the error relative to the activation span
$(L/V)\,(W(b)-W(a))$, over all of them, in the bulk, at the wall and beside the
ball (`postProcessing/radial_errors.dat`).

## Construction

*Reduction.* With $\mathbf M=m\mathbf I$ and $\psi=\psi(r)$,
$\nabla\cdot(\mathbf M\nabla\psi)=m(\psi''+2\psi'/r)$ and
$\sqrt{\nabla\psi\cdot\mathbf M\nabla\psi}=\sqrt m\,|\psi'|$, so that
$c_0\sqrt{\nabla\psi\cdot\mathbf M\nabla\psi}=V|\psi'|$. For $\psi'\ge0$, which holds
on the solution below, the equation with $S_\psi=0$ is

{{< include ../../latex/radial_eikonal_equation.tex >}}

and the sealed wall is $\psi'(R_o)=0$. With $s=r/L$ and the slope $w=V\psi'$
(1 for a plane front) it becomes a linear equation for $w$,

{{< include ../../latex/radial_eikonal_slope_equation.tex >}}

with $w(b)=0$ at the sealed wall.

*Solution of the slope.* The function $u=s^2w$ satisfies

{{< include ../../latex/radial_eikonal_u_equation.tex >}}

which the quadratic

{{< include ../../latex/radial_eikonal_q.tex >}}

solves, and the solutions of the homogeneous equation are multiples of
$e^{\mathrm{Pe}_Ls}$, so $u=q(s)+Ce^{\mathrm{Pe}_Ls}$. The wall condition
$u(b)=0$ fixes $C$. Where $u$ vanishes, $u'=-\mathrm{Pe}_Ls^2<0$, so as $s$
increases $u$ can cross zero only downwards and, being positive just inside
the wall ($u'(b)<0$), stays positive for $s<b$: $w>0$ for $s<b$. The time
follows from $\psi'=w/V$.

*Seed profiles.* The three profiles of the coupler give the same field up to
the value held on the ball. With the critical radius

{{< include ../../latex/radial_eikonal_critical.tex >}}

($r_c=2L/\mathrm{Pe}_L$, and $\rho_c$ is its counterpart in the metric distance
used below), $\psi=T_k$ at $r=R$ for `flat`, $\psi=T_k+R/V$ at $r=R$ for
`front`, and $\psi=T_k$ at $r=r_c$ for `curvedFront`, which is solved in the
field outside $r_c$. The profile `exact` has the field of `flat`; the verifier
holds the ball at it.

*Anisotropy.* A constant anisotropic metric keeps the solution exact in a
stretched coordinate. With the rotation by $\alpha$ about the axis
$(1,1,1)/\sqrt3$,

{{< include ../../latex/radial_eikonal_rotation.tex >}}

($\mathbf K\mathbf v=\mathbf u\times\mathbf v$ for $\mathbf u=(1,1,1)/\sqrt3$) and the
speed ratios $\eta_1,\eta_2,\eta_3$ along the principal axes,

{{< include ../../latex/radial_eikonal_metric.tex >}}

the ball is the ellipsoid $r\le R$ and the wall the ellipsoid $r=R_o$, and the
field of the isotropic problem evaluated at $r=\lVert\boldsymbol\xi\rVert$
solves the equation for $\mathbf M$ between them. The sealed condition
$\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf M\nabla\psi=0$ becomes $\psi'(R_o)=0$: the normal of the
wall is parallel to $\mathbf Q\mathbf D^{-1}\boldsymbol\xi$ and
$\mathbf M\nabla\psi=m\mathbf Q\mathbf D\,\nabla_{\!\xi}\psi$.

## Exact solution

With $q(b)$ the value of $q$ at $s=b$,

{{< include ../../latex/radial_eikonal_slope.tex >}}

and the primitive of $w$ ($W'=w$),

{{< include ../../latex/radial_eikonal_primitive.tex >}}

the field of the problem with $\psi=T_k$ on the ball is

{{< include ../../latex/radial_eikonal_psi.tex >}}

and the three seed profiles are

{{< include ../../latex/radial_eikonal_profiles.tex >}}

The gradient in the anisotropic variant is, with $w$ evaluated at $s=r/L$ and
$\boldsymbol\xi$, $r$ as above,

{{< include ../../latex/radial_eikonal_gradient.tex >}}

which does not depend on the profile. A point inside the ball takes the value
of the ball surface, as the verifier does when it evaluates the error.

*Seed offsets.* The coupler deposits on each
cell of the ball the activation time of its terminal plus an offset that
depends on the metric distance
$\rho=\sqrt{\mathbf d\cdot\mathbf M^{-1}\mathbf d}$ of the cell centre from the
terminal ($\mathbf d$ the offset of the centre from the terminal):

{{< include ../../latex/radial_eikonal_offsets.tex >}}

The `front` offset is $R/V$ at the surface of the ball, the value held for
`front` above. The `curvedFront` offset is zero for $\rho\le\rho_c$ and is the
integral, from $\rho_c$, of $1/c_0+2/(c_0^2\rho)+2/(c_0^3\rho^2)$, the solution
$g$ of $c_0g-g'-2g/\rho=1$ in a medium without a wall.

*Note for implementers.* The NumPy module does not call $\mathrm{Ei}$. It writes
the term of $W$ that contains it as an integral over the wall layer,

{{< include ../../latex/radial_eikonal_primitive_integral.tex >}}

and evaluates the integral by eight-point Gauss--Legendre quadrature on
panels that follow the exponential layer at the wall and the growth of $1/t^2$
at small $t$; `manufacturedRadialEikonalReference.H` does the same. It agrees
with the closed form to $3\times10^{-10}$ for the values of $\mathrm{Pe}_L$ and
$a$ tested below and, unlike the closed form, stays finite for large
$\mathrm{Pe}_L$.

The full expressions are `printed_form()` of `radial_eikonal_mms.py`, whose
closed form is `slope` and `scaled_time` ($=W(s)-W(a)$). The functions of
`reference/radial_eikonal.py` are

- `parameters(c0, m, L)`: $V$ and $\mathrm{Pe}_L$;
- `q(s, Pe)`, `slope(s, Pe, a)` ($w$), `wall_integral(s, Pe, a)` and
  `scaled_time(s, Pe, a)`;
- `exact_time(s, Pe, a, L, V, terminal_time, profile)`, with `profile` one of
  `flat`, `front`, `exact` and `curvedFront`;
- `rotation_about_diagonal(angle)` and `stretched(x, axes, angle)`
  ($\boldsymbol\xi$), with `axes` $=(\eta_1,\eta_2,\eta_3)$;
- `exact_field(x, Pe, a, L, V, terminal_time, profile, axes, angle)` and
  `exact_gradient(x, Pe, a, L, V, axes, angle)`;
- `metric_radius(d, M)` ($\rho$), `seed_offset(rho, c0, profile)` and
  `seed_times(centres, terminal, terminal_time, M, c0, profile)`.

## Self-checks

`--self-check` asserts, for $\mathrm{Pe}_L\in\{2,5,21,46,94\}$ and
$a\in\{0.02,0.1,0.25,0.5\}$ on 40 points above the ball up to the wall:

- the reference slope equals `slope` to $10^{-13}$ and the reference time
  equals `scaled_time`, which uses `scipy.special.expi`, to $3\times10^{-10}$;
- for $a\ge0.1$, the reference slope satisfies the equation for $w$ with
  central differences of step $10^{-5}$ to $10^{-5}$;
- $w$ vanishes at the wall and the time vanishes on the ball, both to
  $10^{-14}$;

and, besides, that:

- where the closed form overflows ($\mathrm{Pe}_L=1000$, $a=0.25$ and
  $\mathrm{Pe}_L=3000$, $a=0.1$) the reference arrival time at the wall is
  finite and equals the integral of the reference slope, by 4000 panels of
  eight-point quadrature, to $10^{-8}$;
- the `front` field exceeds the `flat` field by $(L/V)a$ and the `curvedFront`
  field differs from it by $(L/V)\,(W(a)-W(2/\mathrm{Pe}_L))$ (both to $10^{-14}$),
  the `flat` field is $T_k$ on the ball, and `curvedFront` with
  $a<2/\mathrm{Pe}_L$ is rejected;
- for the anisotropic metric ($c_0=5$, $m=0.5$, $\eta=(1.3,0.8,1.1)$,
  $\alpha=0.7$) at 12 points between the ball and the wall, the exact gradient
  equals central differences of the field to $10^{-6}$, the eikonal residual of the
  field (with the divergence of the flux by central differences) is below
  $10^{-5}$, and $\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf M\nabla\psi$ vanishes on the wall
  ellipsoid to $10^{-12}$;
- the `curvedFront` offset has the slope $1/c_0+2/(c_0^2\rho)+2/(c_0^3\rho^2)$
  to $10^{-6}$ at $c_0=30$, vanishes for $\rho\le\rho_c$, and the `front` and
  `flat` offsets are $\rho/c_0$ and 0.

The expressions printed above are checked against these functions
(`check_printed_form`): with sympy, $w$ solves its equation and vanishes at the
wall, $u$ solves its equation, $q$ solves the equation of $u$, $W'=w$, and
$\psi$ solves the radial equation, is $T_k$ on the ball and has $\psi'=0$ at
$R_o$, `front` is $T_k+R/V$ on the ball and `curvedFront` is $T_k$ at the
critical radius; $VL/\mathrm{Pe}_L=m$, $b=R_o/L$, $r_c=2L/\mathrm{Pe}_L$ and
$\sqrt m\,\rho_c=r_c$. Numerically they equal `slope`, `scaled_time` (also with the wall integral evaluated by
quadrature in place of $\mathrm{Ei}$), `exact_time` for the three profiles,
`seed_offset`, `rotation_about_diagonal`, `stretched` and `exact_gradient`, and
$w>0$ before the wall.

`pytest test_radial_eikonal_mms.py` also compares the emitted module with the
seven self-test samples of the C++ header, which the verifier checks at
start-up as well.

## Regeneration

```bash
python radial_eikonal_mms.py --emit
python radial_eikonal_mms.py --self-check
python radial_eikonal_mms.py --report [--PeL VALUE] [--ballRatio VALUE]
```

`--emit` writes `reference/radial_eikonal.py` and
`latex/radial_eikonal_*.tex`. `--report` prints the arrival time at the wall
and the slope on the ball for the given $\mathrm{Pe}_L$ and $a$. The generator
owns no region of a C++ header: `manufacturedRadialEikonalReference.H` is
hand-written, and the generator tests it through its seven self-test samples
of $w$ and $W(s)-W(a)$. The parity harness of cardiacFoam compares the
compiled header with `reference/radial_eikonal.py` (`mmsParity radial`). The
generator needs SciPy for the closed form; the emitted module does not.
